newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: WILLIAMS NO COMMENT ON THAI-AUSSIE SENTENCE
The Federal Attorney-General, Daryl Williams, won't comment on reports that Federal police were shocked at the severity of the sentence given to three Australians in Thailand this week.
The three were sentenced to 50 years jail each after pleading guilty to attempting to smuggle heroin.
The police officers reportedly described the sentence as inconsistent and draconian, but a spokesman for Mr Williams says as the report doesn't identify the police, he won't respond.
He says Mr Williams' view is that if people are convicted or plead guilty to drug offences they must face the consequences of their actions.
The spokesman says the penalties for drug offences in countries such as Thailand are well-known.
SOME STATES NEED TO DO MORE ON ABORIGINAL HEALTH-WOOLDRIDGE
The Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, says the way to improve Aboriginal health is for the States to provide basic services such as good roads and clean water to Aboriginal communities.
He says the latest report on the health and welfare of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people shows the extent of problems.
The report says indigenous Australians suffer a higher level of illness, and continue to have a much lower life expectancy than the non-indigenous population.
Dr Wooldridge says it will take at least 10 years for any significant improvement, and believes some States have performed poorly in addressing problems.
He says all Aboriginal people want is the same level of services as other Australians.
TRIAL FOR WOMAN ON MURDER AND KIDNAP CHARGES
A 28-year-old woman has been committed to stand trial for the murder of another woman and the kidnapping of her two daughters on Sydney's northern beaches last year.
Michelle McCreight is charged with eleven offences, including the fatal stabbing of 22-year-old Danielle Carole Flood at Dee Why last August.
It's further alleged she kidnapped the dead woman's daughters, Lucinda and Jessie, to avoid apprehension.
Following a two day committal hearing in Sydney's Central Local Court this week, McCreight has been ordered to stand trial in the Supreme Court on a date to be fixed.
FOREIGN AFFAIRS TAKEN TO COMMISSION
A former Foreign Affairs Department officer says he would have been eligible for partner allowances if he'd lived with a woman instead of his gay lover during his London posting.
Forty-four year old Roger Muller is taking his former employer to the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission in Sydney.
He's seeking up to 29-thousand-dollars compensation from the Department, alleging he was discriminated against because he lived with a man during his overseas service.
Mr Muller says the Foreign Affairs and Immigration Departments have since addressed the issue in enterprise bargaining agreements but other departments still discriminate against same-sex couples.
COSTELLO TO ATTEND APEC FINANCE MINISTERS' MEETING
The Federal Treasurer, Peter Costello, will attend the fourth annual APEC Finance Ministers' meeting in the Philippines this weekend.
Mr Costello will also have separate meetings with Treasurers and Finance Ministers from several APEC countries.
THREE PLAYERS SUSPENDED FROM SUPER LEAGUE
In Super League, three players have been suspended after pleading guilty to charges laid after last weekend's round of matches.
The Cowboys' Steve Walters and Penrith's Gordon Falcon each received a one match suspension, while Adelaide's Cameron Blair was outed for two weeks.
However, the Cowboys' John Lomax and Peter Jones, Canterbury's Craig Pollamounter and Darren Britt, and Perth's Mark Geyer have pleaded not guilty and will face the judiciary tomorrow night.
Geyer has pleaded guilty to a high tackle, but wants the offence downgraded, and has pleaded not guilty to an eye gouging charge.
